title: Give a CPR manikin naloxone nasal spray: head held tilted back, nozzle in a nostril up to the flange, one full press
keywords: nozzle in up to the flange
instruction: Give the CPR training manikin one dose from the naloxone nasal spray training device in the holder.
context: About 80,000 people in the US died of opioid overdoses in 2023 (CDC). Naloxone reverses an overdose, and the FDA made NARCAN Nasal Spray an over-the-counter product in 2023 so that bystanders can give it before help arrives; public-health programmes train lay people to use it on CPR manikins with training devices. The package's Quick Start Guide: "Hold the NARCAN Nasal Spray with your thumb on the bottom of the plunger and your first and middle fingers on either side of the nozzle." "Tilt the person's head back and provide support under the neck with your hand. Gently insert the tip of the nozzle into one nostril, until your fingers on either side of the nozzle are against the bottom of the person's nose." "Press the plunger firmly to give the dose." The device fires by a squeeze between plunger and flange, so the holding hand is the firing hand; the head springs back to level unless the other hand holds it tilted.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Adult CPR training manikin (head 19.5 cm long, 15.1 cm wide; firm vinyl), lying face up, top of the head toward the robot: nasal root at x 21.0, y 0, z 22.2 with the head level; nostrils 12 x 8 mm, 8 mm either side of the midline. The head turns on a sprung neck 11 cm behind and 5 cm below the nasal root: tilting it back takes 0.17 N m at the start, 0.81 N m at 23 deg; it stops at 30 deg and springs back to level when let go. Chest and shoulders (fixed) 26 x 40 x 14 cm at x 35 to 61. (2) Naloxone nasal spray training device, NARCAN size: nozzle 15 mm long, 6 mm across; finger flange 42 x 10 x 3 mm; body 16 mm across; plunger with a 28 mm disc, 5 mm stroke, held out by a 15 N spring, clicks at the end; 15 g. It lies in an open holder (7 x 5 cm plate, fixed) at x 20, y -12, its axis along x 2 cm above the table, nozzle toward the robot, the flange across. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A dose is given the first time the plunger reaches the end of its stroke (the click); the device holds one dose, so the score is fixed then. 0 if the nozzle's tip is not at least 3 mm inside a nostril or its axis is more than 20 deg off the nostril's axis (sprayed onto the face). 1.0 if, in addition, the flange or the hand holding the device pressed on the nose (0.5 N or more in the second before the click), the head was tilted back 15 deg or more, and the other hand was on the head (1 N or more). 0.5 if it went into a nostril but any of those three was missing. No click by the end scores 0. Real trial: the click, and a side video for the nozzle, the flange against the nose, the head's tilt (against a protractor card behind the head) and the other hand.
reset_notes: Lay the manikin's head level, put the training device (plunger out, reset) back in its holder, nozzle toward the robot, flange across, wipe the nozzle and the nostril. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The head is rigid (real manikin heads are firm vinyl); its drawn skin is a mesh and it collides as hulls and boxes under it, with 20 mm deep nostril channels. The neck is a sprung hinge (estimate). Device sizes and the 15 N firing force are estimates from the product. No spray is simulated: the dose is the full plunger stroke, scored by where the nozzle is.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (its right gripper knocked the spray out of its holder onto the table and hovered over it; the left arm stayed back; no dose); demo: 1.0
